11 The driver of a car applies two parallel forces to a steering wheel, as shown.
centre of
steering wheel
15 N
65°
65°
15 N
0.40 m
Each force has a magnitude of 15 N and acts in the direction shown. The steering wheel has a
diameter of 0.40 m.
What is the torque exerted on the steering wheel?
A
1.3 N m
B
2.5 N m
C
2.7 N m
D
5.4 N m

hints: Notice the two $15 \text{ N}$ forces are parallel but opposite in turning effect, so they form a couple - add their moments about the centre.
The $0.40 \text{ m}$ diameter is horizontal while each force is at $65^\circ$ to the horizontal, so only the component perpendicular to the diameter contributes to the moment.
Take moments about the centre with radius $0.20 \text{ m}$: each moment is $15 \times 0.20 \times \sin 65^\circ$, then double it for the two sides.
walkthrough: Identify the couple: two equal $15 \text{ N}$ parallel forces act on opposite sides of the wheel of diameter $0.40 \text{ m}$, so radius $r = 0.20 \text{ m}$ from the centre.
State the rule: torque $= F \times$ perpendicular distance from the pivot. For an angled force, use $F_{\perp} = F \sin\theta$ where $\theta$ is the angle to the line joining the force to the pivot.
Here the line from centre to each contact is horizontal and the force is $65^\circ$ to the horizontal, so the perpendicular component is $15 \sin 65^\circ$.
Moment of one force about the centre is $M_1 = 15 \times 0.20 \times \sin 65^\circ \approx 15 \times 0.20 \times 0.9063 \approx 2.72 \text{ N m}$.
Both forces tend to turn the wheel anticlockwise, so total torque $= 2 \times M_1 = 2 \times 2.72 \approx 5.4 \text{ N m}$ with units $\text{N m}$.

A.explanation: This is about half the torque of one correct $15 \text{ N}$ force, from using radius $0.20 \text{ m}$ with $\cos 65^\circ$ instead of the perpendicular separation.

B.explanation: This uses $15 \times 0.40 \times \cos 65^\circ$, the component of force parallel to the separation rather than perpendicular to it.

C.explanation: This is the correct torque from only one $15 \text{ N}$ force, $15 \times 0.20 \times \sin 65^\circ \times 2$ is needed or $15 \times 0.40 \times \sin 65^\circ$ for the couple.

D.explanation: The couple gives $15 \times 0.40 \times \sin 65^\circ \approx 5.4 \text{ N m}$, with both forces turning the wheel the same way.
